extracted.intended_audience: academics, empirical economists, IP scholars, and policymakers studying patent examination quality and labor behavior (including USPTO researchers and staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical evaluation of patent examiner behavior and examination quality using PAIR transaction-level data; tests for procrastination (end-loading) and its consequences (allowance rates, rework, delays), exploiting quotas and telecommuting as identification strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence of Application End-loading (FOAM completed on last day of quota period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the first office action on the merits (FOAM) for an application is completed and processed on the last day of the bi-weekly (or quarterly) quota period. The authors report that roughly half of FOAMs are completed on the last day of the quota period and document 26 evenly spaced spikes corresponding to bi-weekly deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by counting FOAM completions by calendar day and by days prior to quota-period ends (histograms, averaging across periods). Used as the primary marker of 'end-loading' and initial empirical indicator of possible procrastination. Analysis includes day-level frequency histograms and regression outcomes; weekend dips and quarter-end spikes should be accounted for.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-Office-Action (FOAM) Allowance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The incidence/probability that the FOAM results in allowance (i.e., the patent is allowed on the first substantive report). The paper finds the rate of allowance on the FOAM is drastically lower for applications reviewed near quota deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome metric for assessing rushed or low-quality first actions ('shotgun' behavior). Analyzed in regressions controlling for examiner fixed effects, year effects, and covariates; differences in FOAM allowance by timing (end-loaded vs non-end-loaded) are interpreted as consistent with time-inconsistent behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence of Second-Office-Action Non-Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the second office action issued by the examiner is a non-final rejection (i.e., the examiner issues a subsequent non-final rejection, indicating new grounds were raised after FOAM). The paper treats such second non-final rejections as an indicator of low-quality initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as evidence that the FOAM failed to include all bases for rejection (incomplete review). Regression analyses examine the relationship between FOAM end-loading and the likelihood of a second non-final rejection; standard errors clustered at the examiner level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence of Ultimate Application Allowance (Final Disposition Allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the application is ultimately allowed by the end of prosecution (final disposition), regardless of FOAM outcome. Used to see whether end-loaded/shotgun rejections are later overcome and whether ultimate grant rates differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compared across end-loaded vs non-end-loaded FOAMs to assess whether initial low-quality FOAMs are corrected in later rounds; included as regression outcome with controls and fixed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence of Application Being Allowed at both the EPO and JPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same underlying invention was eventually allowed at both the European Patent Office (EPO) and the Japan Patent Office (JPO). Used as a cross-office validation measure of application merit/quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a falsification / external validity metric: higher cross-office allowance incidence suggests stronger underlying merit; regressions on this outcome help assess whether timing effects reflect application quality or examiner behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence of Request for Continued Examination (RCE) and Number of RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether applicants filed a Request for Continued Examination and the count/log number of such requests for a given application. RCEs indicate additional prosecution effort often arising from prior rejections or continued contestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an indicator of additional rounds of examination (rework) potentially triggered by low-quality initial FOAMs. Regressions evaluate association between end-loading and RCE incidence/number; results interpreted as costs of end-loading on future workload and applicant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Duration (Time between Filing and Final Disposition, in days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the entire examination period measured in days from filing to final disposition. The paper finds end-loading is associated with longer overall examination durations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify delay costs attributed to end-loading/procrastination. Analyses include OLS and IV regressions (instrumenting end-loaded indicator with examiner mean end-loading rate) and include examiner and year fixed effects and covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shotgun Rejection (low-quality, quick rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concept/quality category: a 'shotgun' rejection is a quick, low-quality (potentially invalid) rejection issued under time pressure, e.g., rejecting claims as non-novel even though cited prior art may not disclose the invention. Examiners may use such rejections near quota deadlines because FOAM rejections are non-final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified indirectly via lower FOAM allowance rates at deadline, higher second non-final rejections, higher RCEs, and longer ultimate examination durations. The paper theorizes shotgun rejections are preferred over improper allowances because they buy time for later review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quota Compliance / Bi-weekly and Quarterly Counts (Work Credits / Counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected number of work credits ('counts') examiners must earn over bi-weekly and quarterly periods; quotas vary by technology complexity and GS pay grade. Credits historically earned upon issuance of FOAM and at final disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the benchmark/no-procrastination counterfactual: non-procrastinating examiners should roughly smooth work over the bi-week, whereas procrastinators cluster near period ends. Quotas create the framework to detect end-loading. Consider GS-level signatory authority and partial credits (post-2010 changes) when interpreting counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Telecommuting Status (treatment in quasi-experiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether the application was reviewed while the assigned examiner was telecommuting; telecommuting rollout across examiners is used as a staggered natural experiment to test effects of reduced supervision on end-loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event-study design: regress end-loading and quality outcomes on leads/lags of examiner commencement of telecommuting, with examiner and year fixed effects and covariates. Telecommuting is theorized to exacerbate self-control problems (increase end-loading and shotgun behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-Level End-loading Rate (mean end-loading rate among examiner's other applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average propensity of an examiner to end-load FOAMs across the year (excluding the application at hand). Used as an instrument (or moderator) for whether a specific FOAM is end-loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employed as an instrument for application-level end-loading in IV analyses to estimate causal effects on outcomes (FOAM allowance, ultimate allowance, second non-final rejection, examination duration). Also interacted with application-level end-loading dummy to assess heterogeneous effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-Order/Falsification Variables: Immutable Application Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Application-level immutable characteristics used in falsification exercises (e.g., applicant entity size, priority status, whether filed at EPO/JPO prior to U.S. filing). The paper uses these to check that end-loading patterns are not driven by sorting on immutable application traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as control variables and outcomes in regressions to falsify alternative (time-consistent) explanations like application sorting; lack of correlation between end-loading and these immutable traits supports procrastination interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day-level FOAM Frequency Distribution / Bunching Intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive metric: histograms/density plots of FOAM completions across days within the bi-weekly period (and over calendar years) showing bunching patterns (spikes at period ends and quarter ends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to visualize and quantify the extent and periodicity of end-loading (bi-week spikes, weekend effects, increased intensity near quarter-end). Useful for initial diagnosis and to motivate regression specifications.
